lines.text: Keep clear of the falls. Lifeboats don't launch for empty pockets.
lines.journalNote: Bosun Hari guards the starboard davits like a warden. Thick rope and knotted muscle.

lines.text: The barometer's in the basement. Something ugly is coming up through the floorboards.
lines.journalNote: Hari senses the impending mutiny. He checks his cleaver and tightens the lifeboat winch.

lines.text: Kedar runs the deck now. I don't care whose head is on the sovereign, so long as it weighs true.
lines.journalNote: Hari switched allegiance to Kedar without blinking. Coin is his only creed.

lines.text: The cutter's our only chance! The winch is locked—you hold the release plate, I'll grease the gears!
lines.journalNote: Hari panics as the ship shudders. He yells that the winch plate will drop the lifeboat.

lines.text: One gold coin from the captain's stash. Bring me that, and this cutter drops into the swell with you in it.
lines.journalNote: Hari named his price: one gold coin from the captain's chest to launch the escape cutter.

lines.text: Saw something shining near the capstan. Silver locket. Left it alone. Dead men's trinkets bring bad water.
lines.journalNote: Hari mentioned a silver locket lying on the deck near the main capstan.

lines.text: Quartermaster. Six silver sovereigns in your pouch, right? Drop three in my palm and you'll find this boat unlashed when you need it.
lines.journalNote: Hari knows the Quartermaster has coin and openly offered a deal for lifeboat access.

lines.text: Navigator, if this tub cracks in half, you'd better know which star points to shallow reef. Lifeboats don't sail themselves.
lines.journalNote: Hari warned the Navigator that charts mean nothing without an open sea.

lines.text: Step away from the gunwale, rat. You don't have the coin to look at these oars.
lines.journalNote: Hari shoved me back from the lifeboats with a grunt of contempt.

lines.text: You heard me the first time. Keep moving.
I'm not here for idle chatter, swab. The cutter stays lashed.
Beat it before I take a belaying pin to your ribs.
Ropes don't lie. When the hemp frays this fast, the sea's hungry.
A lifeboat is six planks between you and the abyss. Don't look at it unless you can pay.
I don't trust the calm. The sea always smiles sweetest right before she snaps.
The davits are greased, but the winch is stiff. Takes iron will to lower them into this swell.
Gold doesn't drown. Men do. Remember that if the timbers start groaning.
I've seen mutinies before. They always end with red water and empty hammocks.
Keep your hands off the lanyards. One false knot and the boat flips on the falls.
The water smells like dead kelp and copper tonight. Cursed water.
You've got that look in your eye. Like a man who already knows which wave has his name on it.
If the ship goes, stay off the rigging. The masts go down first.
I've coiled rope on twenty vessels. None ever groaned with this tone.
A marlinspike solves more arguments than a parley. Don't test me.
